summary: The no-reuse transport decision keys off the call's intent, not its HTTP method (Codex gocli1219-r3 P1): attemptHTTPClient sends every call that is not replay-safe through the keep-alive-free HTTP/1 client when it carries a per-call key (any method; mutationCarriesCallKey is method-independent) or when its wire method is one Go's transport resends on its own (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE: goTransportReplaysMethod), so a keyed or unkeyed state-changing GET (GetMutatingWithHeaders, doMutation) never reaches a reusable connection. The other method-based replay decisions now read the intent too: the config-level key-header strip, the CLI-generated key, and the cross-origin redirect refusal (a mutating GET is never sent to another origin).
reason: r3 decided the keyed no-reuse client and the key strip by isReadMethod, so a keyed mutating GET stayed on the pooled HTTP/1 mutation client where Go may resend a GET on a dead reused connection.
validated_outcome: TestKeyedMutatingGETDroppedAfterAWarmCallIsSentOnce (one keyed /drop hit, fresh connection) and TestNoReuseClientIsChosenByIntentForEveryMethod (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, keyed and streaming; unkeyed replayable methods) fail on the r3 code and pass; TestMutatingGETIsNeverRedirectedCrossOrigin pins the redirect rule.
